# A `#id` may be duplicated, and a body rendered more than once may read its
# handles: each copy reads its own.
#
# uniqueNodeIDs renames the later copies of an id and lets the first keep the
# name, so a test naming `#inc` still means the `#inc` it wrote. A read cannot
# follow that rename -- the checker declares one var per written id and every
# spliced copy shares it -- so a prop read is answered in the body before the
# splice (passNodePropReads), and `{bar.text}` in each copy is that copy's
# "b{n}". read.sngl's test clicks the first copy's button and reads both.
#
# An unbound two-way prop's cell is answered per copy too, by the inliner
# (instance_state_read_runs.txt).

sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out read.sngl
sngl test --platform=none read.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go read.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

# A method called through the handle is a call of the node, which
# repointHandleCalls points at each copy's own: `bar.pulse()` in each copy of
# dup.sngl pulses its own bar.
#
# The rename is keyed by name and the refusal by symbol, and they are different
# questions: the rename repairs the emitted namespace, where any two `#bar`s
# collide, while the refusal is about a read that cannot say which copy it
# meant, which only arises within one body. innocent.sngl is the difference.

sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out1 dup.sngl
grep 'WidgetPulse\(m\.bar\)' out1/main.go
grep 'WidgetPulse\(m\.bar__1\)' out1/main.go

# Two unrelated components may each write `#bar`. `reader` is rendered once and
# is the only thing that reads it; `quiet` is rendered twice and reads nothing.
# Neither var satisfies both halves, so this compiles. Keyed by name it was
# refused -- and the message then asserted that a component rendered once
# renders more than one.
sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out2 innocent.sngl
grep 'WidgetPulse\(m\.bar\)' out2/main.go
grep 'bar__1 ' out2/main.go
grep 'bar__2 ' out2/main.go

# The same program with `quiet`'s id spelled differently. This is the pair that
# keeps the keying honest: the two differ only in a name that `reader`'s read was
# never bound to, so a symbol-keyed refusal cannot tell them apart and both
# compile. If a future change rejoins the two by spelling, exactly one of this
# pair goes red.
sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out3 renamed.sngl
grep 'WidgetPulse\(m\.bar\)' out3/main.go
grep 'baz ' out3/main.go
grep 'baz__1 ' out3/main.go

# One instance is the ordinary case: the handle is the program's var, and the
# action's receiver reaches it.
sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out4 single.sngl
grep 'WidgetPulse\(m\.bar\)' out4/main.go

-- read.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

component bump ui.node {
    var n = 0
    ui.vbox {
        ui.button #bar(text="b{n}", @click { n += 1 })
        ui.text #out(value="{bar.text}")
    }
}

component pair ui.node {
    ui.vbox {
        bump #one()
        bump #two()
    }
}

ui.window {
    pair()
}

func testEachCopyReadsItsOwn(t test.Test, c pair) {
    c.one.bar.click()
    t.assert(c.one.out.value == "b1")
    t.assert(c.two.out.value == "b0")
}
-- dup.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:time"
import gtk "gir:Gtk-4.0"

output {
    go {
        gtk4
    }
}

component bump() node {
    gtk.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.0) {}

    time.timer(interval=100ms, @tick {
        bar.pulse()
    })
}

window {
    vbox {
        bump()
        bump()
    }
}
-- innocent.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:time"
import gtk "gir:Gtk-4.0"

output {
    go {
        gtk4
    }
}

component reader() node {
    gtk.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.0) {}

    time.timer(interval=100ms, @tick {
        bar.pulse()
    })
}

component quiet() node {
    gtk.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.5) {}
}

window {
    vbox {
        reader()
        quiet()
        quiet()
    }
}
-- renamed.sngl --

import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:time"
import gtk "gir:Gtk-4.0"

output {
    go {
        gtk4
    }
}

window {
    vbox {
        gtk.GtkProgressBar #bar(fraction=0.0) {}
        time.timer(interval=100ms, @tick {
            bar.pulse()
        })
    }
}
